html:
Scam-Kit Fingerprinting API: Turn Any Phishing Link Into a Matchable Kit Identity

Every phishing wave you've ever investigated reuses the same kits. Tycoon 2FA, Evilginx, Sneaky 2FA, Darcula: the adversary-in-the-middle panels behind smishing links are built once and deployed thousands of times. Only the per-victim nonces and rotated credentials change between sightings.

Today RelayShield is launching scam-kit fingerprinting as a pay-as-you-go API: submit one suspicious link, get back a stable, deterministic kit identity. A kit_sha256 fingerprint ID that is identical for the same kit across every sighting, even when every credential on the page has rotated.

Why this didn't exist before

Kit analysis lived in two places: academic prototypes with no hosted API, and enterprise brand-protection suites where kit-signature detection is buried inside expensive contracts. Nobody sold kit fingerprinting as a per-call API. So we built it: deterministic IDs, per-call pricing, on the same Stripe and x402 (USDC) rails as the rest of our API.

What the fingerprint captures

Our v1 fetch pipeline records what the kit's server actually does:

  • Up to 5 redirect hops: the chains behind Evilginx rickroll lures and W3LL Wikipedia-antibot pages fire dedicated behavior classes in the fingerprint itself
  • Response headers, including kit tells like X-Evilginx
  • TLS facts measured against the kit host: negotiated version, cipher, certificate issuer, SANs, certificate age
  • Up to 2 bounded secondary fetches (Evilginx canary check, remote favicon), each hashed and recorded

And one honesty rule we're proud of: we never compute JA3/JA4 locally. JA3/JA4 fingerprint the TLS client (our fetcher), not the kit server. If you have your own proxy, EDR, or IdP telemetry, pass it in and it's recorded verbatim, marked caller-supplied, never presented as server-measured.

Secrets, tokens, and machine identifiers are stripped before hashing, so two kits differing only in rotated credentials fingerprint identically. Kit families resolve against 20 approved names (Tycoon 2FA, Evilginx, Sneaky 2FA, Mamba 2FA, EvilProxy, FlowerStorm, Rockstar 2FA, NakedPages, W3LL Panel, Greatness, Caffeine, SessionShark, Darcula, Irontoll, Wazza, N0va, Ghostcode, Knight-Office, Milk-Dragon, PhantomSub); anything else is marked suggested until a human approves it. A no-hit result always says "no flags found", never "safe".

Pricing

  • $0.50: fingerprint a kit (/v1/payg/scamkit-fingerprint)
  • $0.10: match a fingerprint ID against the corpus (/v1/payg/scamkit-match)
  • $5.50 flat: campaign scan across up to 25 indicators (/v1/payg/campaign-scan)
  • $199/month flat monthly pricing: all 30 endpoints, 500 pooled executions/month, $0.40 overage

Pay per call with x402 (USDC) or Stripe. The same corpus backs it: 123 monitored Telegram marketplaces, 661K+ indicators, 8.4M+ citations.

Try it

The endpoints are live now. See pricing and grab an API key at api.relayshield.net/developers. Fingerprint your first suspicious link for fifty cents and see whether the kit behind it has been seen before.
